packs.description: CAN-SPAM Act rules for commercial email compliance covering sender identification, opt-out requirements, content labeling, and prohibited practices
CCPA/CPRA rules covering consumer rights, Do Not Sell requirements, privacy policy obligations, and sensitive personal information
COPPA rules for children's online privacy protection covering parental consent, privacy notices, data security, and age screening requirements
FTC Endorsement Guides and advertising rules covering endorsements, claims, disclosures, and consumer protection
GDPR rules covering consent, privacy policies, data subject rights, and international transfers
HIPAA Privacy and Security rules covering PHI protection, consent requirements, and privacy notices
SEC Rule 482 - Investment Company Advertising rules covering performance data, fee disclosures, risk statements, and prospectus requirements
SEC Marketing Rule 206(4)-1 - Investment adviser advertising rules covering testimonials, endorsements, performance, ratings, and hypothetical returns

rules.title: Transactional Email Definition
rules.summary: Transactional or relationship messages (order confirmations, account updates, warranty info) are exempt from most CAN-SPAM requirements, but must not be deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Transactional emails are exempt from opt-out and identification requirements, but the primary purpose must genuinely be transactional. Do not disguise commercial messages as transactional.

rules.title: Primary Purpose Test
rules.summary: If an email contains both transactional and commercial content, the primary purpose determines whether CAN-SPAM applies. Commercial content in subject line makes it commercial.

remediation.guidance: When mixing transactional and commercial content, the primary purpose determines classification. If the subject line or opening content is commercial, the entire message is commercial under CAN-SPAM.

rules.title: Accurate Header Information
rules.summary: Header information in commercial email must not be materially false or misleading. From, To, Reply-To, and routing information must be accurate.

remediation.guidance: Ensure From, To, Reply-To, and routing information accurately identifies the person or business who initiated the email.

rules.title: Non-Deceptive Subject Lines
rules.summary: Subject lines must not be deceptive or misleading about the content of the message.

remediation.guidance: Subject lines must accurately reflect the content of the email. Do not use deceptive subject lines like fake Re: or Fwd: prefixes.

rules.title: Advertisement Identification
rules.summary: Commercial email must be clearly and conspicuously identified as an advertisement or solicitation.

remediation.guidance: Include clear identification that the message is a commercial advertisement or solicitation, unless the recipient has given prior affirmative consent.

rules.title: Physical Postal Address
rules.summary: Commercial email must include a valid physical postal address of the sender.

remediation.guidance: Include a valid physical postal address in every commercial email. This can be a street address, P.O. Box, or private mailbox registered with a commercial mail receiving agency.

rules.title: Opt-Out Mechanism Required
rules.summary: Every commercial email must include a clear and conspicuous mechanism to opt out of future messages.

remediation.guidance: Include a clear, conspicuous, and functional opt-out mechanism in every commercial email. Must be operational for at least 30 days after sending.

rules.title: Honor Opt-Out Requests
rules.summary: Opt-out requests must be honored within 10 business days. Cannot send commercial email after opt-out request is received.

remediation.guidance: Process opt-out requests within 10 business days. Once a recipient opts out, stop sending them commercial email. The opt-out mechanism must remain functional for at least 30 days.

rules.title: Free Opt-Out
rules.summary: Cannot charge a fee, require the recipient to provide information beyond email address, or make the recipient take more than a single step to opt out.

remediation.guidance: Opt-out must require no more than a single action (e.g., clicking a link or sending a reply). Cannot require login, payment, or additional personal information beyond email address.

rules.title: No Selling Opt-Out Lists
rules.summary: Cannot sell, transfer, or share email addresses of recipients who have opted out.

remediation.guidance: Never sell, lease, exchange, or otherwise transfer the email addresses of people who have opted out of your messages.

rules.title: No Dictionary Attacks
rules.summary: Cannot generate email addresses using automated tools that combine names, letters, or numbers (dictionary attacks).

remediation.guidance: Do not use automated tools to generate email addresses by combining names, letters, numbers, or other characters. All recipient addresses must be legitimately obtained.

rules.title: No Harvested Addresses
rules.summary: Cannot send commercial email to addresses obtained through automated harvesting of websites or online services.

remediation.guidance: Only send commercial email to addresses obtained through legitimate means (direct opt-in, business relationship). Never use harvested, scraped, or purchased email lists.

rules.title: Sender Identification
rules.summary: The sender of commercial email must be clearly identifiable. The 'From' line must accurately identify the person or entity who initiated the message.

remediation.guidance: Clearly identify the sender in the 'From' field. If sending on behalf of another party, both the sender and the party must be identified.

rules.title: Sexually Explicit Content
rules.summary: Email with sexually explicit content must include 'SEXUALLY-EXPLICIT:' at the beginning of the subject line and specific initial viewable content requirements.

remediation.guidance: If sending email with sexually explicit content, include 'SEXUALLY-EXPLICIT:' at the beginning of the subject line and ensure no sexually explicit content appears in the initial viewable area.

rules.title: Pre-Collection Disclosure
rules.summary: Businesses must provide notice at or before the point of collection of personal information.

remediation.guidance: Provide notice at point of collection listing categories and purposes.

rules.title: Right to Know What Is Collected
rules.summary: Consumers have the right to know what personal information is collected about them.

remediation.guidance: Disclose categories of personal information collected and purposes.

rules.title: Right to Delete
rules.summary: Consumers have the right to request deletion of personal information collected from them.

remediation.guidance: Provide clear mechanism to request deletion and respond within 45 days.

rules.title: Specific Pieces of Information
rules.summary: Consumers have the right to request specific pieces of personal information collected about them.

remediation.guidance: Implement process to provide specific data upon verified request.

rules.title: Minors Consent Required
rules.summary: Businesses must obtain affirmative opt-in consent before selling personal information of consumers under 16 years of age.

remediation.guidance: Implement age verification and obtain consent for minors data sale.

rules.title: Right to Opt-Out of Sale
rules.summary: Consumers have the right to opt-out of the sale or sharing of their personal information.

remediation.guidance: Implement opt-out mechanism and honor requests immediately.

rules.title: Non-Discrimination
rules.summary: Businesses cannot discriminate against consumers for exercising their CCPA rights.

remediation.guidance: Do not deny services, charge different prices, or provide different quality based on privacy choices.

rules.title: Request Methods
rules.summary: Businesses must provide two or more designated methods for consumers to submit requests, including at minimum a toll-free telephone number and website address.

remediation.guidance: Provide toll-free number and website form for privacy requests.

rules.title: Response Timeline
rules.summary: Businesses must respond to verifiable consumer requests within 45 days of receipt.

remediation.guidance: Implement process to acknowledge receipt and respond within 45 days.

rules.title: Do Not Sell Link Required
rules.summary: Businesses that sell personal information must provide a clear and conspicuous link titled 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' or 'Do Not Share My Personal Information' on their homepage.

keywords: do not sell my personal information
do not share my personal information

remediation.guidance: Add visible "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" link in website footer.

rules.title: Privacy Policy Requirements
rules.summary: Businesses must update their privacy policy at least once every 12 months and include CCPA-required disclosures.

remediation.guidance: Update privacy policy annually with CCPA-required disclosures.

rules.title: Sensitive Personal Information
rules.summary: Under CPRA, businesses must provide consumers the right to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information.

keywords: limit the use of my sensitive personal information

remediation.guidance: Provide "Limit Use of My Sensitive Personal Information" link if applicable.

rules.title: Data Retention Limits
rules.summary: Must retain children's personal information only as long as reasonably necessary to fulfill the purpose for which it was collected.

remediation.guidance: Delete children's personal information once it is no longer reasonably necessary. Do not retain it indefinitely.

rules.title: Notice on Website/App
rules.summary: Operators of websites or online services directed to children under 13 must post a clear, prominent, and complete online privacy notice.

remediation.guidance: Post a clearly labeled, complete children's privacy notice linked from every page that collects information from children.

rules.title: Verifiable Parental Consent
rules.summary: Must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using, or disclosing personal information from children under 13.

remediation.guidance: Obtain verifiable parental consent using an approved method (signed form, credit card, video conference, etc.) before collecting data from children under 13.

rules.title: Content of Privacy Notice
rules.summary: Children's privacy notice must list categories of personal information collected, how it is used, disclosure practices, and contact information for the operator.

keywords: categories of information collected from children

remediation.guidance: Include in the notice: operator contact info, categories of data collected from children, how data is used, disclosure practices, and parental rights.

rules.title: Direct Notice to Parents
rules.summary: Must provide direct notice to parents before collecting information from their child, describing what information will be collected and how it will be used.

remediation.guidance: Send direct notice to parents describing what data will be collected, how it will be used, and how parents can provide or revoke consent.

rules.title: Consent Methods
rules.summary: Verifiable parental consent must use a method reasonably calculated to ensure the consenting person is the child's parent.

remediation.guidance: Use an FTC-approved consent verification method: signed form returned by mail/fax/email scan, credit card transaction, video conference, or government ID check.

rules.title: Parental Rights
rules.summary: Parents must be able to review personal information collected from their child, request deletion, and refuse further collection.

remediation.guidance: Provide parents the ability to: (1) review their child's personal information, (2) request deletion, and (3) refuse further collection or use.

rules.title: No Conditioning on Data Collection
rules.summary: Cannot condition a child's participation in an activity on providing more personal information than is reasonably necessary.

remediation.guidance: Do not require children to disclose more information than is reasonably necessary to participate in an activity. Only collect what is strictly needed.

rules.title: Data Security
rules.summary: Must establish and maintain reasonable procedures to protect the confidentiality, security, and integrity of children's personal information.

remediation.guidance: Implement reasonable data security measures to protect children's personal information from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.

rules.title: Age Screening
rules.summary: Sites directed to a general audience that knowingly collect information from children under 13 must implement age screening.

remediation.guidance: Implement age screening before collecting personal information. If a user indicates they are under 13, block data collection or trigger parental consent flow.

rules.title: Educational Technology Exception
rules.summary: Schools may consent on behalf of parents for educational technology services, but only for school-authorized educational purposes.

remediation.guidance: When relying on school consent, use collected data only for school-authorized educational purposes. Do not use for commercial purposes.

rules.title: Safe Harbor Programs
rules.summary: Operators may participate in FTC-approved self-regulatory safe harbor programs as an alternative to individual FTC enforcement.

remediation.guidance: Consider joining an FTC-approved COPPA safe harbor program (CARU, kidSAFE, PRIVO, iKeepSafe) for additional compliance support.

rules.title: Former Price Comparisons
rules.summary: Price comparisons to a "former price" must be based on actual prices at which the item was offered in good faith for a reasonably substantial period.

remediation.guidance: Only show "was $X" prices that reflect genuine prior pricing. Maintain records of historical pricing.

rules.title: Comparable Value Claims
rules.summary: Retail value or comparable value claims must accurately reflect the price at which comparable products are sold by others.

remediation.guidance: Verify comparable prices before using "Retail Value" or "Compare at" claims. Document competitive pricing.

rules.title: Manufacturer List Price Claims
rules.summary: Claims of savings from manufacturer's list price or suggested retail price must reflect prices at which products are actually sold.

remediation.guidance: Only reference MSRP if products are actually sold at that price in the market.

rules.title: Bargain Offers Based on Other Purchases
rules.summary: Offers like "Buy one, get one free" must not inflate the price of the first item to recover the cost of the "free" item.

remediation.guidance: In BOGO offers, the first item price must be the regular price. Do not inflate to cover free item.

rules.title: No Bait Advertising
rules.summary: Bait advertising is an alluring but insincere offer to sell a product which the advertiser does not intend to sell.

remediation.guidance: Ensure advertised products are available in reasonable quantities. Do not use low prices just to lure customers.

rules.title: No Bait and Switch
rules.summary: It is deceptive to disparage the advertised product, fail to show it, or refuse to take orders for it in order to switch consumers to a higher-priced item.

remediation.guidance: Honor advertised prices. Do not discourage purchase of advertised items to upsell alternatives.

rules.title: Must Have Adequate Supply
rules.summary: Advertisers must have adequate supply of advertised products to meet reasonably anticipated demand.

remediation.guidance: Stock sufficient inventory for advertised offers. If limited, clearly disclose quantity available.

rules.title: No Refusal to Sell Advertised Item
rules.summary: Refusal to show, demonstrate, or sell the advertised product is evidence of bait advertising.

remediation.guidance: Train staff to actively sell advertised products. Do not create obstacles to purchasing advertised items.

rules.title: "Free" Offer Conditions Must Be Disclosed
rules.summary: All conditions and obligations for receiving a "free" item must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Disclose all conditions upfront: "Free with $50 purchase" not hidden in fine print.

rules.title: No Continuous "Free" Offers
rules.summary: "Free" offers cannot be used continuously - they must be intermittent to preserve the meaning of "free."

remediation.guidance: Limit duration of free offers. A perpetual "free gift" promotion is deceptive.

rules.title: "Free" Must Be Genuinely Free
rules.summary: The word "Free" may only be used when the consumer pays nothing for the item and is not required to purchase anything else at an inflated price.

remediation.guidance: Only use "FREE" when the item is truly free with no hidden costs or inflated companion purchase requirements.

rules.title: "Free" Cannot Inflate Regular Price
rules.summary: The regular price of merchandise sold with a "free" offer must not be increased to cover the cost of the free item.

remediation.guidance: Maintain regular pricing during free promotions. Do not mark up base product to cover "free" item costs.

rules.title: "Free" Item Shipping Charges
rules.summary: Shipping and handling charges for a "free" item must be reasonable and disclosed. Excessive S&H that covers item cost is deceptive.

remediation.guidance: If charging S&H for "free" items, charges must be reasonable and clearly disclosed before checkout.

rules.title: Endorsement Guide Purpose
rules.summary: The FTC Endorsement Guides address the application of Section 5 of the FTC Act to endorsements and testimonials in advertising.

remediation.guidance: Understand that endorsement guidelines apply to all advertising mediums including social media.

rules.title: Endorsement Guide Scope
rules.summary: FTC Endorsement Guides apply to endorsements and testimonials in advertising.

remediation.guidance: Apply these guidelines to all endorsements in marketing materials.

rules.title: Current User Requirement
rules.summary: Endorsers must be bona fide users of the product at time of endorsement.

remediation.guidance: Ensure endorsers are current users of the product or service.

rules.title: Endorsements Must Reflect Honest Opinions
rules.summary: Endorsements must reflect the honest opinions, findings, beliefs, or experience of the endorser.

remediation.guidance: Ensure all endorsements are genuine and reflect actual user experience. Do not script or fabricate testimonials.

rules.title: Endorsements Cannot Be Misleading
rules.summary: Endorsements may not contain any representations that would be deceptive or could not be substantiated if made directly by the advertiser.

remediation.guidance: Verify that all claims in endorsements can be substantiated. Remove unverifiable statements.

rules.title: Claim Substantiation
rules.summary: Claims in endorsements must be substantiated by the advertiser.

remediation.guidance: Verify all claims made in endorsements are accurate and can be proven.

rules.title: Atypical Results Require Disclosure
rules.summary: If an endorsement represents results that are not typical, the advertiser must clearly disclose expected results for consumers.

remediation.guidance: Include clear disclosure of typical results when showing exceptional testimonials. Example: "Results not typical. Most users see [X]."

rules.title: Actor Portrayal Requires Disclosure
rules.summary: If the person appearing in an advertisement is not an actual consumer, this must be clearly disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose "Actor portrayal" or "Dramatization" when not using actual customers.

rules.title: Consumer Endorser Must Be Actual User
rules.summary: An advertisement using an endorsement by a consumer must use an actual consumer of the product or service.

remediation.guidance: Only use endorsements from people who have actually used the product. Actors portraying consumers must be disclosed.

rules.title: Consumer Endorsement Disclosure
rules.summary: Consumer endorsements should clearly disclose what the typical consumer experience is.

remediation.guidance: Include clear disclosure of typical outcomes alongside testimonials.

rules.title: Typical Results Disclosure
rules.summary: If results are not typical, must clearly disclose expected results or that results may vary.

remediation.guidance: Add "Results not typical" or disclose generally expected results.

rules.title: Expert Must Actually Evaluate Product
rules.summary: Experts must actually exercise their expertise in evaluating the product features relevant to their endorsement.

remediation.guidance: Document that expert endorsers have conducted actual evaluation using their professional expertise.

rules.title: Expert Endorsers Must Be Qualified
rules.summary: An expert endorser must possess the expertise represented by the endorsement and must have actually evaluated the product.

remediation.guidance: Verify expert credentials. Ensure expert has actually examined/tested the product before endorsing.

rules.title: Expert Qualification
rules.summary: Expert endorsers must have qualifications to give expert opinion on the subject.

remediation.guidance: Verify expert credentials match the subject matter of endorsement.

rules.title: Organization Endorsement Standards
rules.summary: Organization endorsements must represent the collective judgment of the organization, not just individual members.

remediation.guidance: Ensure organization endorsements follow proper approval processes and reflect collective judgment.

rules.title: Affiliate Link Disclosure
rules.summary: Affiliate links and commission arrangements must be disclosed when recommending products.

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose affiliate relationships. Example: "This post contains affiliate links. I may earn a commission."

rules.title: Clear and Conspicuous Disclosure
rules.summary: Disclosures must be clear, conspicuous, and hard to miss.

remediation.guidance: Place disclosures prominently, not buried in text. Use clear language like "#ad" or "Paid partnership".

rules.title: Material Connection Disclosure
rules.summary: Material connections between endorsers and advertisers must be clearly disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Disclose any payment, free products, employment, or business relationship.

rules.title: Disclosure Must Be Clear and Conspicuous
rules.summary: Disclosures must be clear, conspicuous, and placed where consumers will notice them before engaging with the endorsement.

remediation.guidance: Place disclosures at the beginning of content. Use clear language like "Ad" or "Sponsored". Avoid burying in hashtags.

rules.title: Employee Endorser Disclosure
rules.summary: Employees who endorse products in their personal capacity must disclose their employment relationship.

remediation.guidance: Require employees posting about company products to clearly disclose their employment.

rules.title: Free Product Disclosure
rules.summary: If an endorser received a free product to review, this must be clearly disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Include clear disclosure when products were provided for free. Example: "Product provided for review."

rules.title: Material Connection Disclosure Required
rules.summary: When there is a material connection between an endorser and seller that would affect the weight of the endorsement, it must be disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Disclose all material connections: payments, free products, employment, family relationships, equity stakes.

rules.title: Social Media Disclosure
rules.summary: Social media posts by paid influencers must clearly disclose the material connection.

remediation.guidance: Use #ad or "Sponsored" at the beginning of posts, not hidden in hashtags.

rules.title: Advertiser Liable for Endorser Claims
rules.summary: Advertisers are liable for false or unsubstantiated statements made by endorsers, and for failing to disclose material connections.

remediation.guidance: Monitor endorser content. Provide clear guidelines to endorsers. Require compliance training.

rules.title: Advertiser Must Monitor Endorsers
rules.summary: Advertisers must take steps to monitor endorsers and address non-compliant content.

remediation.guidance: Implement monitoring program for influencer and affiliate content. Address violations promptly.

rules.title: Green Guides Purpose
rules.summary: The Green Guides help marketers avoid making environmental claims that are unfair or deceptive under Section 5 of the FTC Act.

remediation.guidance: Environmental marketing claims must be truthful, substantiated, and not misleading.

rules.title: Non-Toxic Claims
rules.summary: Non-toxic claims must be substantiated for all foreseeable human and environmental exposures.

remediation.guidance: Substantiate non-toxic claims with testing. Consider all exposure routes and populations.

rules.title: Recyclable Claims
rules.summary: Recyclable claims should be qualified if recycling facilities are not available to a substantial majority of consumers.

remediation.guidance: Qualify recyclable claims: "Recyclable where facilities exist" or "Check local recycling." Specify which components.

rules.title: Recycled Content Claims
rules.summary: Recycled content claims must specify whether content is pre-consumer or post-consumer recycled material.

remediation.guidance: Distinguish between pre-consumer and post-consumer recycled content. Specify percentage accurately.

rules.title: Renewable Energy Claims
rules.summary: Renewable energy claims must be substantiated. If using RECs, marketers should not overstate environmental benefits.

remediation.guidance: Distinguish between on-site generation and REC purchases. Disclose methodology.

rules.title: Renewable Materials Claims
rules.summary: Renewable materials claims should not be deceptive about the overall environmental benefit.

remediation.guidance: Specify what percentage of materials are from renewable sources. Identify the renewable materials.

rules.title: Environmental Claims Must Be Substantiated
rules.summary: All environmental claims must be substantiated by competent and reliable scientific evidence.

remediation.guidance: Maintain documentation supporting all environmental claims. Claims should be specific and verifiable.

rules.title: Qualify Broad Environmental Claims
rules.summary: Broad environmental claims should be qualified to prevent deception about the product's environmental attributes.

remediation.guidance: Avoid vague claims like "eco-friendly". Use specific claims like "Made with 50% recycled plastic."

rules.title: General Environmental Benefit Claims
rules.summary: Unqualified general environmental benefit claims (e.g., "green" or "eco-friendly") are difficult to substantiate and should be avoided.

remediation.guidance: Replace vague environmental claims with specific, measurable benefits that can be documented.

rules.title: Carbon Offset Claims
rules.summary: Carbon offset claims must reflect genuine, verifiable, permanent emission reductions and should be properly qualified.

remediation.guidance: Use third-party verified carbon offsets. Disclose offset methodology and certifying body.

rules.title: Environmental Certifications and Seals
rules.summary: Environmental certifications and seals can be deceptive if they imply general environmental benefit without qualification.

remediation.guidance: Clarify what specific attribute the certification covers. Disclose certifying organization.

rules.title: Compostable Claims
rules.summary: Compostable claims should specify whether the item is suitable for home composting or requires industrial facilities.

remediation.guidance: Specify composting conditions: "Commercially compostable only" or "Home compostable." Include timeframe if relevant.

rules.title: Degradable and Biodegradable Claims
rules.summary: Degradable claims require evidence that the product will completely break down within one year under normal disposal conditions.

remediation.guidance: Only claim biodegradable if product fully decomposes within 1 year. Qualify for specific disposal conditions.

rules.title: Free-Of Environmental Claims
rules.summary: Free-of claims must be truthful and should not be made if the substance was never present or associated with the product category.

remediation.guidance: Only claim "free of X" if (1) X is typically present in similar products, and (2) absence provides environmental benefit.

rules.title: Difficult Cancellation Process
rules.summary: Cancellation must be as easy as sign-up. Complex cancellation processes (call-only, multiple steps, retention offers) violate FTC guidelines.

remediation.guidance: Provide simple online cancellation option. Do not require phone calls or multiple retention attempts.

rules.title: Superlative Claims Without Basis
rules.summary: Claims like "best", "#1", "leading", or "top-rated" require substantiation through comparative testing or market data.

remediation.guidance: Remove unsubstantiated superlative claims or provide evidence (market share data, comparative tests, awards).

rules.title: "Clinically Proven" Without Clinical Trials
rules.summary: Claims like "clinically proven" or "clinically tested" require actual clinical trials supporting the specific claim.

remediation.guidance: Remove "clinically proven" unless backed by published, peer-reviewed clinical trials. Cite specific studies.

rules.title: "Doctor Recommended" Without Substantiation
rules.summary: Claims like "doctor recommended" or "#1 doctor choice" must be based on actual surveys or endorsements from qualified medical professionals.

remediation.guidance: Remove doctor recommendation claims or provide substantiation (survey methodology, sample size, date).

rules.title: "100% Guaranteed" Claims
rules.summary: Absolute guarantee claims must be honored and any conditions must be clearly disclosed.

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose all conditions, limitations, and procedures for any guarantee. Honor all guarantees offered.

rules.title: Unsubstantiated Health Benefit Claims
rules.summary: Health benefit claims (cures, treats, prevents disease) require competent and reliable scientific evidence.

remediation.guidance: Remove unsupported health claims. Use qualified language like "may support" with appropriate disclaimers.

rules.title: Specific Percentage Efficacy Claims
rules.summary: Specific percentage claims (e.g., "90% effective", "reduces wrinkles by 50%") require supporting evidence.

remediation.guidance: Substantiate percentage claims with studies or testing. Include methodology and conditions.

rules.title: "Scientifically Proven" Without Studies
rules.summary: Claims invoking scientific authority must be supported by actual scientific studies relevant to the claim.

remediation.guidance: Remove scientific proof claims or cite specific peer-reviewed studies with links to publications.

rules.title: Unsubstantiated Weight Loss Claims
rules.summary: Claims like "Lose X pounds in Y days" require competent and reliable scientific evidence. Most rapid weight loss claims are deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Remove specific weight loss claims unless supported by clinical trials. Add disclaimer about typical results and need for diet/exercise.

rules.title: Dark Pattern: Difficult Cancellation
rules.summary: Making cancellation significantly harder than sign-up is a deceptive dark pattern.

remediation.guidance: Implement "click-to-cancel" - online cancellation should be as easy as online sign-up.

rules.title: Dark Pattern: Confirmshaming
rules.summary: Using manipulative language to shame users out of declining offers is a deceptive dark pattern.

remediation.guidance: Use neutral opt-out language. Replace "No, I don't want savings" with "No thanks" or "Decline".

rules.title: Dark Pattern: Hidden Costs at Checkout
rules.summary: Revealing hidden fees, taxes, or charges only at checkout is a deceptive drip pricing dark pattern.

remediation.guidance: Display total price including all mandatory fees upfront. No surprise charges at checkout.

rules.title: Dark Pattern: Visual Misdirection
rules.summary: Using visual tricks (fake X buttons, disguised ads, misleading buttons) to manipulate user choices is deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Ensure all UI elements behave as expected. Close buttons should close, not redirect.

rules.title: Dark Pattern: Pre-Selected Add-Ons
rules.summary: Pre-checking boxes for add-ons, insurance, or upgrades without user action is a deceptive dark pattern.

remediation.guidance: Do not pre-select any optional add-ons. Let users affirmatively choose extras.

rules.title: Hidden Conditions for "Free" Products
rules.summary: Offers of "free" products with hidden conditions (shipping, subscription, purchase requirement) must clearly disclose all terms.

remediation.guidance: Disclose all conditions for "free" offers prominently and before checkout. E.g., "Free with $50 purchase" not just "FREE".

rules.title: Free Trial Auto-Charge Without Disclosure
rules.summary: Free trials that automatically convert to paid subscriptions must clearly disclose the conversion terms before enrollment.

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose before checkout: (1) Free trial length, (2) Post-trial price, (3) How to cancel. Get affirmative consent.

rules.title: Carbon Neutral Without Certification
rules.summary: Carbon neutral and carbon offset claims should be substantiated with reliable third-party certification.

remediation.guidance: Provide certification details for carbon neutral claims. Disclose offset methodology and certifier.

rules.title: Misleading Biodegradable Claims
rules.summary: "Biodegradable" claims require evidence that the product completely breaks down within one year under normal disposal conditions.

remediation.guidance: Substantiate biodegradable claims with testing. Specify timeframe and disposal conditions.

rules.title: Unsubstantiated Eco-Friendly Claims
rules.summary: Broad environmental claims like "eco-friendly" or "green" must be qualified and substantiated.

remediation.guidance: Replace vague "eco-friendly" with specific, substantiated claims (e.g., "Made with 50% recycled content").

rules.title: Misleading Natural or Organic Claims
rules.summary: "Natural" and "organic" claims should be specific and substantiated. For food/cosmetics, USDA standards may apply.

remediation.guidance: Specify what makes the product natural. For organic claims, obtain USDA certification if applicable.

rules.title: Unqualified Recyclable Claims
rules.summary: "Recyclable" claims must specify what parts are recyclable and whether recycling facilities are available to consumers.

remediation.guidance: Qualify recyclable claims: specify which parts, include recycling instructions, note facility availability.

rules.title: Vague Sustainable Claims
rules.summary: Broad claims like "sustainable" should be qualified with specific, substantiated environmental benefits.

remediation.guidance: Replace vague sustainability claims with specific achievements (e.g., "Made with 100% renewable energy").

rules.title: Missing Advertisement Label
rules.summary: Native ads must include clear and prominent disclosure that identifies them as advertising.

remediation.guidance: Add clear "Ad" or "Advertisement" label in a prominent location using contrasting text.

rules.title: Sponsored Content Disguised as Editorial
rules.summary: Paid content that mimics editorial content must be clearly identified as advertising.

remediation.guidance: Clearly label sponsored content with "Advertisement", "Sponsored", or "Paid Content" in prominent placement.

rules.title: Negative Option / Subscription Trap
rules.summary: Subscription services must clearly disclose terms and obtain express informed consent before charging. Silence cannot equal consent.

remediation.guidance: Before charging, clearly disclose: (1) Total cost, (2) Recurring nature, (3) Cancellation method. Require checkbox consent.

rules.title: Hidden Recurring Charges
rules.summary: Recurring charges must be clearly disclosed upfront, not hidden in fine print or terms of service.

remediation.guidance: Display recurring charge amount and frequency prominently near the price and in checkout summary.

rules.title: Employee/Insider Reviews Without Disclosure
rules.summary: Reviews from employees, owners, or business insiders must clearly disclose the material connection.

remediation.guidance: Require all employee reviewers to prominently disclose their employment relationship.

rules.title: Fake or AI-Generated Reviews
rules.summary: Using fake, fabricated, or AI-generated reviews to deceive consumers is prohibited. Reviews must reflect genuine consumer experiences.

remediation.guidance: Remove all fake or AI-generated reviews. Only display authentic customer reviews with verified purchases.

rules.title: Incentivized Reviews Without Disclosure
rules.summary: Offering discounts, free products, or other incentives for reviews without clear disclosure violates FTC guidelines.

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose when reviews are incentivized with labels like "Incentivized Review" or "Received free product for review."

rules.title: Review Manipulation / Cherry-Picking
rules.summary: Displaying only positive reviews, hiding negative reviews, or manipulating the order of reviews to mislead consumers is deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Display reviews objectively. Allow consumers to sort by rating including negative reviews.

rules.title: Fake Review Counts or Star Ratings
rules.summary: Displaying fake or inflated review counts, star ratings, or aggregate scores is deceptive advertising.

remediation.guidance: Ensure all displayed ratings and review counts accurately reflect actual verified customer reviews.

rules.title: Review Gating / Selective Review Solicitation
rules.summary: Soliciting reviews only from satisfied customers or filtering out negative reviews before they are posted is deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Solicit reviews from all customers equally. Do not screen or gate reviews based on expected rating.

rules.title: Fabricated High Demand Claims
rules.summary: Claims like "selling fast" or "X people viewing" that are fabricated or manipulated are deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Only display real-time data that is accurate. Remove if viewer counts or demand claims are fabricated.

rules.title: False Exclusivity Claims
rules.summary: Claims of exclusivity ("exclusive offer", "invitation only") that are not genuine are deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Remove false exclusivity claims. Only use "exclusive" for genuinely limited or member-only offers.

rules.title: Perpetual Sale / False Deadline
rules.summary: Running perpetual "sales" or claiming "sale ends today" when it does not is deceptive pricing.

remediation.guidance: Only advertise sales with genuine end dates. Document regular vs. sale pricing periods.

rules.title: False Low Stock Claims
rules.summary: Claims like "Only X left!" or "Low stock" that are false or manipulated to create urgency are deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Only display stock counts that reflect actual inventory. Remove if counts are fabricated or artificially limited.

rules.title: Fake Countdown Timers
rules.summary: Countdown timers that reset, extend, or do not reflect real deadlines are deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Remove countdown timers unless they reflect genuine time-limited offers. Do not reset timers.

rules.title: "Assembled in USA" Misuse
rules.summary: "Assembled in USA" requires principal assembly in the US. Must not imply higher US content than exists.

remediation.guidance: Only use "Assembled in USA" if significant assembly occurs in the US. Disclose foreign components.

source.citation: FTC Act §5 / Made in USA Policy

rules.title: Country of Origin Misrepresentation
rules.summary: Misrepresenting country of origin through flags, symbols, or misleading statements is deceptive.

remediation.guidance: Accurately represent country of origin. Do not use US flags/symbols for foreign-made products.

rules.title: Unqualified "Made in USA" Claim
rules.summary: Unqualified "Made in USA" claims require that the product be "all or virtually all" made in the United States.

remediation.guidance: Verify that final assembly and all significant parts/processing are in the USA. If not, qualify the claim.

source.citation: FTC Act §5 / Made in USA Policy

rules.title: No Bait and Switch
rules.summary: Advertising an offer that is not genuinely available to lure customers is illegal.

remediation.guidance: Ensure advertised products/prices are actually available to consumers.

rules.title: Hidden Fee Disclosure
rules.summary: All material fees must be clearly disclosed upfront, not hidden.

remediation.guidance: Disclose all fees prominently before purchase. No surprise charges.

rules.title: Truth in Advertising
rules.summary: Advertising must be truthful, not misleading, and backed by evidence.

remediation.guidance: Substantiate all advertising claims before making them.

rules.title: Response to Requests
rules.summary: Controllers must respond to data subject requests within one month.

remediation.guidance: Implement process to handle and respond to data subject requests within 30 days.

rules.title: Transparent Information
rules.summary: Information about data processing must be provided in a concise, transparent, intelligible form using clear and plain language.

remediation.guidance: Use clear, simple language in privacy notices. Avoid legal jargon.

rules.title: Right to Lodge Complaint
rules.summary: Must inform data subjects of their right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

remediation.guidance: Inform data subjects of their right to complain to a supervisory authority and provide contact details.

rules.title: Controller Identity Disclosure
rules.summary: At data collection, must disclose identity and contact details of the controller.

remediation.guidance: Include company name, address, and contact information in privacy notice.

rules.title: Legitimate Interest Disclosure
rules.summary: When processing is based on legitimate interests, the specific interests must be identified and disclosed.

remediation.guidance: When relying on legitimate interests as a legal basis, specify the actual interests pursued. Generic statements like 'our legitimate interests' are insufficient.

rules.title: Purpose and Legal Basis Disclosure
rules.summary: Must disclose purposes and legal basis for processing at collection.

remediation.guidance: Clearly state why data is being collected and the legal basis.

rules.title: Recipients Disclosure
rules.summary: Must disclose the recipients or categories of recipients of personal data at the time of collection.

remediation.guidance: Disclose all recipients or categories of recipients who will receive personal data.

rules.title: Retention Period Disclosure
rules.summary: Must disclose how long personal data will be stored or criteria for determining retention.

remediation.guidance: Include data retention periods in privacy policy.

rules.title: Indirect Data Collection Disclosure
rules.summary: When personal data is not obtained directly from the data subject, must disclose the source and categories of data within a reasonable period.

remediation.guidance: Disclose the source of personal data when it was not collected directly from the data subject, including the categories of data obtained.

rules.title: Right of Access
rules.summary: Data subjects have the right to obtain confirmation and access to their personal data.

remediation.guidance: Inform users of their access rights and provide mechanism to request data.

rules.title: Right to Erasure
rules.summary: Data subjects have the right to have their personal data erased in certain circumstances.

remediation.guidance: Inform users of their erasure rights and provide deletion request mechanism.

rules.title: Right to Data Portability
rules.summary: Data subjects have the right to receive their data in a machine-readable format.

remediation.guidance: Provide data export functionality in common formats (JSON, CSV).

rules.title: Right to Object to Marketing
rules.summary: Data subjects have an absolute right to object to direct marketing at any time.

remediation.guidance: Provide easy opt-out from all marketing communications.

rules.title: Right to Object
rules.summary: Data subjects have the right to object to processing based on legitimate interests.

remediation.guidance: Inform users of their right to object and provide mechanism to do so.

rules.title: Automated Decision-Making Disclosure
rules.summary: Data subjects have the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling. Must disclose existence of automated decision-making and meaningful information about the logic.

remediation.guidance: Disclose existence of automated decision-making, meaningful information about the logic involved, and the significance and envisaged consequences.

rules.title: Lawful, Fair, and Transparent Processing
rules.summary: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner.

remediation.guidance: Ensure clear legal basis for processing and transparent communication.

rules.title: Purpose Limitation
rules.summary: Personal data must be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes.

remediation.guidance: Clearly state purposes at collection and do not process for incompatible purposes.

rules.title: Legal Basis Required
rules.summary: Processing must have a valid legal basis: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.

remediation.guidance: Document and disclose the legal basis for each processing activity.

rules.title: Consent Conditions
rules.summary: Where consent is the legal basis, controller must demonstrate the data subject consented.

remediation.guidance: Keep records of consent including when, how, and what was consented to.

rules.title: Cookie Consent Banner
rules.summary: Non-essential cookies require explicit consent before being set.

remediation.guidance: Implement cookie consent banner that blocks non-essential cookies until consent.

rules.title: Unbundled Consent
rules.summary: Consent requests must be clearly distinguishable from other matters. Consent cannot be bundled into terms of service or pre-ticked.

keywords: by using this site you agree

remediation.guidance: Present consent requests separately from terms of service. Do not use pre-ticked boxes. Consent must be a clear affirmative action.

rules.title: Right to Withdraw Consent
rules.summary: Data subjects must be able to withdraw consent as easily as they gave it.

remediation.guidance: Provide clear and easy mechanism to withdraw consent at any time.

rules.title: Children's Data Consent
rules.summary: Processing personal data of children under 16 requires parental consent. Information society services directed at children must verify age and obtain parental authorization.

remediation.guidance: Implement age verification mechanisms and obtain verifiable parental consent for children under 16.

rules.title: Special Categories of Data
rules.summary: Processing of special category data (health, biometric, genetic, racial/ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, sexual orientation) requires explicit consent.

remediation.guidance: Obtain explicit consent before processing special category data. Clearly disclose what special categories are processed and why.

rules.title: International Data Transfer Disclosure
rules.summary: Must disclose intention to transfer data to third countries and safeguards in place.

remediation.guidance: Disclose international transfers in privacy policy with legal mechanisms used.

rules.title: Access Control Requirements
rules.summary: Technical policies must limit access to ePHI to authorized persons.

remediation.guidance: Implement unique user IDs, automatic logoff, and encryption.

rules.title: Audit Controls
rules.summary: Hardware, software, and procedures must record and examine access to ePHI.

remediation.guidance: Implement audit logging for all ePHI access and review logs regularly.

rules.title: ePHI Encryption
rules.summary: Electronic PHI must be encrypted when transmitted over networks.

remediation.guidance: Use TLS/HTTPS for all ePHI transmission. Encrypt data at rest.

rules.title: Marketing Use Restrictions
rules.summary: PHI may not be used for marketing purposes without explicit authorization.

remediation.guidance: Obtain written authorization before using PHI for any marketing activities.

rules.title: Minimum Necessary Standard
rules.summary: Covered entities must make reasonable efforts to limit PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.

remediation.guidance: Implement policies to limit PHI access and disclosure to minimum necessary.

rules.title: Permitted Uses and Disclosures
rules.summary: PHI may only be used or disclosed as permitted or required by the Privacy Rule.

remediation.guidance: Ensure all PHI uses and disclosures fall within permitted categories.

rules.title: Authorization Form Elements
rules.summary: Authorization forms must contain specific required elements including description of PHI, purpose, and expiration.

remediation.guidance: Include all required elements: PHI description, purpose, expiration, right to revoke.

rules.title: Authorization Required for Marketing
rules.summary: Written authorization is required before using PHI for marketing communications.

remediation.guidance: Implement authorization forms that meet HIPAA requirements for marketing.

rules.title: Privacy Notice Content Requirements
rules.summary: Notice must describe uses/disclosures, individual rights, and entity duties.

remediation.guidance: Include all required content: uses, disclosures, rights, complaints process.

rules.title: Notice of Privacy Practices Required
rules.summary: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Privacy Practices describing how PHI may be used.

remediation.guidance: Display Notice of Privacy Practices prominently and provide copy to patients.

rules.title: Website Privacy Notice
rules.summary: Entities with websites must post Notice of Privacy Practices prominently online.

remediation.guidance: Post full Notice of Privacy Practices on website and link from all PHI collection pages.

rules.title: Individual Access Rights
rules.summary: Individuals have the right to access and obtain copies of their PHI.

remediation.guidance: Implement process to handle access requests within 30 days.

rules.title: Electronic Access
rules.summary: If PHI is maintained electronically, individuals may request electronic copies.

remediation.guidance: Provide electronic copies in requested format if readily producible.

rules.title: Sanctions Policy
rules.summary: Covered entities must have sanctions against workforce members who violate privacy policies.

remediation.guidance: Document and enforce sanctions policy for privacy violations.

rules.title: Workforce Training
rules.summary: Covered entities must train workforce members on privacy policies and procedures.

remediation.guidance: Implement regular HIPAA training and document completion.

rules.title: Secure PHI Collection Forms
rules.summary: Web forms collecting PHI must use secure transmission and link to privacy notice.

remediation.guidance: Use HTTPS for all forms. Link to Notice of Privacy Practices near PHI fields.

rules.title: Tracking Technology on Health Pages
rules.summary: Third-party tracking pixels on pages with PHI may constitute unauthorized disclosure.

remediation.guidance: Remove or limit third-party trackers on pages collecting or displaying health information.

rules.title: General Advertisement Requirements
rules.summary: Advertisements for investment companies must comply with SEC Rule 482 requirements, including required disclosures and prohibitions on misleading content.

remediation.guidance: Ensure all fund advertisements contain required disclosures and are not misleading.

rules.title: Prospectus Availability Statement
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must include a statement directing investors to carefully consider objectives, risks, charges, and expenses in the prospectus.

remediation.guidance: Include: "Consider the investment objectives, risks, charges, and expenses carefully before investing. The prospectus contains this and other information. Read it carefully."

rules.title: Most Recent Calendar Quarter
rules.summary: Performance data in investment company advertisements must be updated to the most recent calendar quarter-end and include an 'as of' date.

remediation.guidance: Update performance data quarterly. Include "as of" date for all performance figures.

rules.title: Gross vs Net Performance
rules.summary: When showing gross performance, investment company advertisements must also show net-of-fee performance to avoid misleading investors.

remediation.guidance: Show net-of-fee performance alongside any gross performance figures.

rules.title: Required Performance Periods
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements showing performance must include 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year (or since inception if shorter) average annual total returns.

remediation.guidance: Include 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year (or since inception) average annual total returns.

rules.title: Standardized Performance Required
rules.summary: All performance data in investment company advertisements must use SEC-standardized total return calculations.

remediation.guidance: Use SEC-standardized total return calculations for all performance data.

rules.title: Expense Ratio Disclosure
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must disclose the total annual fund operating expense ratio from the most recent prospectus.

remediation.guidance: Include total annual fund operating expense ratio from the most recent prospectus.

rules.title: Sales Load Disclosure
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must disclose maximum sales charges (loads), including both front-end and back-end loads, or clearly state if the fund is no-load.

remediation.guidance: Disclose maximum front-end and back-end sales loads, or clearly state "no-load" if applicable.

rules.title: Tax Impact Disclosure
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements showing performance must disclose whether figures are pre-tax or after-tax and explain relevant tax implications.

remediation.guidance: Disclose whether performance figures are pre-tax or after-tax, and explain tax implications.

rules.title: Not FDIC Insured Statement
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must clearly state that the fund is not FDIC insured, has no bank guarantee, and may lose value.

remediation.guidance: Include: "Not FDIC Insured • No Bank Guarantee • May Lose Value"

rules.title: Principal Risk Statement
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must include a statement that investment return and principal value will fluctuate, and shares may be worth more or less than original cost when redeemed.

remediation.guidance: Include: "Investment return and principal value will fluctuate. Shares, when redeemed, may be worth more or less than their original cost."

rules.title: Average Annual Total Returns
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must calculate and present average annual total returns using SEC-standardized methodology.

remediation.guidance: Calculate and present average annual total returns using SEC-standardized methodology.

rules.title: Benchmark Comparison
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements showing performance should include comparison to an appropriate benchmark index for the same time periods.

remediation.guidance: Include comparison to an appropriate benchmark index for the same time periods.

rules.title: Current Performance Availability
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must provide a phone number or website URL where investors can obtain current month-end performance data.

remediation.guidance: Include phone number or website URL where current month-end performance can be obtained.

rules.title: Past Performance Legend
rules.summary: Investment company advertisements must include a clear statement that past performance does not guarantee future results.

remediation.guidance: Include: "Past performance does not guarantee future results."

rules.title: No Misleading Implications
rules.summary: Advertisement must not include statements that would be otherwise misleading or deceptive by implication

remediation.guidance: Review all statements for potential misleading implications even if technically true.

rules.title: No Material Omissions
rules.summary: Advertisement must not omit any material fact that would make the advertisement misleading

remediation.guidance: Include all material facts necessary for complete understanding of advertised services.

rules.title: No Untrue Statements
rules.summary: Advertisement must not include any untrue statement of a material fact

remediation.guidance: Verify all factual claims in marketing materials. Remove or correct any untrue statements.

rules.title: Bad Actor Disqualification
rules.summary: Persons subject to bad actor disqualifications may not provide testimonials or endorsements

remediation.guidance: Screen all testimonial/endorsement providers for bad actor disqualifications.

rules.title: Endorsement Disclosure Requirements
rules.summary: Endorsements must clearly disclose any compensation paid and conflicts of interest

remediation.guidance: Clearly disclose any compensation paid for endorsements and any conflicts of interest.

rules.title: Promoter Requirements
rules.summary: Investment advisers must execute written promoter agreements and implement oversight procedures

remediation.guidance: Execute written promoter agreements and implement oversight procedures.

rules.title: Testimonial Disclosure Requirements
rules.summary: Testimonials must include disclosure of client status, compensation received, and material conflicts of interest

remediation.guidance: Disclose: (1) client status, (2) compensation received, (3) material conflicts of interest.

rules.title: Third-Party Rating Disclosures
rules.summary: Third-party ratings must disclose the date, period evaluated, identity of rater, and any compensation paid

remediation.guidance: Include: date of rating, period evaluated, identity of rater, and any compensation paid.

rules.title: Rating Questionnaire Disclosure
rules.summary: Must disclose if rating was based on self-reported questionnaire data

remediation.guidance: Disclose if rating was based on self-reported questionnaire data.

rules.title: Composite Performance Requirements
rules.summary: Must create composites of similar strategy accounts rather than showing cherry-picked account performance

remediation.guidance: Create composites of similar strategy accounts rather than showing cherry-picked account performance.

rules.title: Gross and Net Performance
rules.summary: Must show net performance alongside gross performance with equal prominence

remediation.guidance: Always show net performance alongside gross performance with equal prominence.

rules.title: Portable Performance Attribution
rules.summary: Portable track record must clearly identify the responsible person and prior firm

remediation.guidance: Ensure portable track record clearly identifies the responsible person and prior firm.

rules.title: Performance Time Periods
rules.summary: Must include standardized 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year (or since inception) returns

remediation.guidance: Include standardized 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year (or since inception) returns.

rules.title: Hypothetical Performance Disclosures
rules.summary: Hypothetical performance must be clearly labeled and disclose assumptions, limitations, and that it does not reflect actual trading

remediation.guidance: Label as hypothetical. Disclose: (1) assumptions used, (2) limitations, (3) that it does not reflect actual trading.

rules.title: Hypothetical Performance Requirements
rules.summary: Restrict hypothetical performance to sophisticated audiences and include all limitations and assumptions

remediation.guidance: Restrict hypothetical performance to sophisticated audiences. Include all limitations and assumptions.

rules.title: Extracted Performance Disclosure
rules.summary: When showing performance of a subset, must also show the total portfolio performance

remediation.guidance: When showing performance of a subset, also show the total portfolio performance.

rules.title: Predecessor Performance Requirements
rules.summary: Must clearly identify predecessor entity and verify substantially similar investment process

remediation.guidance: Clearly identify predecessor entity and verify substantially similar investment process.

rules.title: Related Performance Requirements
rules.summary: Must explain material differences between the related strategy shown and the strategy being offered

remediation.guidance: Explain material differences between the related strategy shown and the strategy being offered.
